title: Briggs's inequality for polynomials with only negative zeros
statement:
Let $f(x)=\sum_{l=0}^{n}a_lx^l$ be a polynomial with nonnegative coefficients, and suppose that all zeros of $f(x)$ are negative. **Briggs's conjecture.** For $1\leq l\leq n-1$, one has

$$
a_{l-1}a_{l+2}^2+a_l^2a_{l+3}+a_{l+1}^3>a_{l+1}(a_{l-1}a_{l+3}+2a_la_{l+2}),
$$

and

$$
a_l^2(a_l^2-a_{l-1}a_{l+1})>a_{l-1}^2(a_{l+1}^2-a_la_{l+2}).
$$

The conjecture is the polynomial inequality underlying the Briggs inequalities studied for partition and overpartition functions; the supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.16185

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2024).
source_name: Xin-Bei Liu and Zhong-Xue Zhang, “The Briggs inequality for partitions and overpartitions”, arXiv:2408.16185 (2024).
